| E01 | In the labeled line list, how many female cases were hospitalized? | 1 (`"GENDER" = 'Female' AND "hosp_yn" = 'Yes'`) |
| E02 | In the labeled line list, how many cases had a lower-middle socioeconomic status? | 10 (`"ses_cat" = 'Lower-middle'`) |
| E03 | In the labeled line list, how many cases had an upper-middle or high socioeconomic status? | 8 (`"ses_cat" IN ('Upper-middle', 'High')`) |

The truth counts were computed over the CSV while planning (`ses_cat` 1: 6, 2: 10, 3: 5, 4: 3), and the truth test checks each against the coded line list's own count, so a conversion bug shows up as a truth failure before any model runs. /**
```ts
 * A dataset the eval database loads, from a CSV under its data directory.
 * A column with `sourceSql` is filled by that SQL over the CSV's columns,
 * as a converted column is; any other is the CSV's value cast to its type.
 */
type EvalDataset = Pick<CovidDataset, "id" | "fileName" | "truthViewName"> & {
  columns: ReadonlyArray<{ name: string; dataType: string; sourceSql?: string }>;
};

function _buildCreateTableSql(dataset: EvalDataset, dataDir: string): string {
  const castColumns = dataset.columns
    .map((column) => {
      const duckDbType = DUCKDB_TYPE_BY_APP_TYPE[column.dataType] ?? "VARCHAR";
      const valueSql =
        column.sourceSql ?? `CAST("${column.name}" AS ${duckDbType})`;
      return `${valueSql} AS "${column.name}"`;
    })
    .join(", ");
```

```ts
import { ColumnConversion } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/ColumnConversion/ColumnConversion";
import type { ColumnCodes } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/ColumnCodes/ColumnCodes";
import type { DataDictionaryCodeList } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionaryCodeList/DataDictionaryCodeList";
import type { CovidDataset } from "../covid/covidWorkspace";

/** A coded line list's dataset, with the code lists a dictionary attaches. */
export type MeaslesDataset = Omit<CovidDataset, "columns"> & {
  columns: ReadonlyArray<{
    name: string;
    dataType: string;
    codes?: ColumnCodes.Context;
    /**
     * The SQL that fills a converted column from the CSV. Left out, the
     * column is the CSV's value cast to `dataType`.
     */
    sourceSql?: string;
  }>;
};

/** One code and its label, with no other spellings. */
function _createCodePair(
  code: string,
  label: string,
  isMissing = false,
): DataDictionaryCodeList.Pair {
  return { code, label, acceptedSpellings: [], isMissing };
}

const CASE_ID_DESCRIPTION = "Case number assigned by the reporting county.";
const GENDER_DESCRIPTION = "Sex recorded on the case report.";
const HOSPITALIZED_DESCRIPTION =
  "Admitted to a hospital for at least one night.";

/** 9 has no label yet, as a dictionary learned from data can leave it. */
const SEX_PAIRS = [
  _createCodePair("1", "Male"),
  _createCodePair("2", "Female"),
  _createCodePair("9", ""),
];
const YES_NO_PAIRS = [_createCodePair("Y", "Yes"), _createCodePair("N", "No")];
const SES_PAIRS = [
  _createCodePair("1", "Low"),
  _createCodePair("2", "Lower-middle"),
  _createCodePair("3", "Upper-middle"),
  _createCodePair("4", "High"),
];

/**
 * The SQL a linked dataset's view decodes a column with: the app's own
 * `CASE`, through `ColumnConversion`, so the eval converts exactly as the
 * app does. The CSV holds no unmatched value, so nothing is kept.
 */
function _buildDecodeSql(
  columnName: string,
  pairs: readonly DataDictionaryCodeList.Pair[],
  isOrdered: boolean,
): string {
  return ColumnConversion.toCaseSql({
    valueSql: `"${columnName}"`,
    conversion: {
      datasetColumnId: columnName,
      direction: "decode",
      pairs,
      isOrdered,
      overrides: [],
      keepsOriginalAs: undefined,
      outputDataType: "varchar",
      inputDataType: undefined,
    },
    keptValues: [],
  });
}

/** The line list with a dictionary attached as reference. */
const CODED_LINE_LIST: MeaslesDataset = {
  id: "5e1b7c2a-8d4f-4a6e-9b3c-2f7d1e0a4c58",
  name: "measles-line-list-small.csv",
  fileName: "measles-line-list-small.csv",
  truthViewName: "line_list",
  columns: [
    {
      name: "case_id",
      dataType: "varchar",
      codes: { direction: "decode", pairs: [], description: CASE_ID_DESCRIPTION },
    },
    {
      name: "GENDER",
      dataType: "bigint",
      codes: { direction: "decode", pairs: SEX_PAIRS, description: GENDER_DESCRIPTION },
    },
    {
      name: "hosp_yn",
      dataType: "varchar",
      codes: {
        direction: "decode",
        pairs: YES_NO_PAIRS,
        description: HOSPITALIZED_DESCRIPTION,
      },
    },
    {
      name: "ses_cat",
      dataType: "bigint",
      codes: { direction: "decode", pairs: SES_PAIRS },
    },
    { name: "onset_dt", dataType: "date" },
    { name: "county", dataType: "varchar" },
  ],
};

/**
 * The line list's linked dataset: the same rows with GENDER, hosp_yn, and
 * ses_cat converted to labels. Each converted column's codes say it holds
 * labels (`encode`), as the app's loaders describe a converted column.
 */
const LABELED_LINE_LIST: MeaslesDataset = {
  id: "8c4e2f1a-3b7d-4e9a-a6c5-1d2f3e4a5b6c",
  name: "measles-line-list-small (labeled)",
  fileName: "measles-line-list-small.csv",
  truthViewName: "labeled_line_list",
  columns: [
    {
      name: "case_id",
      dataType: "varchar",
      codes: { direction: "decode", pairs: [], description: CASE_ID_DESCRIPTION },
    },
    {
      name: "GENDER",
      dataType: "varchar",
      sourceSql: _buildDecodeSql("GENDER", SEX_PAIRS, false),
      codes: { direction: "encode", pairs: SEX_PAIRS, description: GENDER_DESCRIPTION },
    },
    {
      name: "hosp_yn",
      dataType: "varchar",
      sourceSql: _buildDecodeSql("hosp_yn", YES_NO_PAIRS, false),
      codes: {
        direction: "encode",
        pairs: YES_NO_PAIRS,
        description: HOSPITALIZED_DESCRIPTION,
      },
    },
    {
      name: "ses_cat",
      dataType: "varchar",
      sourceSql: _buildDecodeSql("ses_cat", SES_PAIRS, true),
      codes: { direction: "encode", pairs: SES_PAIRS },
    },
    { name: "onset_dt", dataType: "date" },
    { name: "county", dataType: "varchar" },
  ],
};

/**
 * The coded-columns workspace: the 24-row measles line list the e2e tests
 * import, with a dictionary attached as reference, and its linked dataset
 * converted to labels.
 */
export const MEASLES_DATASETS: readonly MeaslesDataset[] = [
  CODED_LINE_LIST,
  LABELED_LINE_LIST,
];
```

### Task 25: End-to-end: a linked dataset

One test, driven through the UI with only the dictionary seeded before the first page load. A workspace owner imports the line list, opens **Apply a dictionary** from its ⋯ menu (which now promises to turn codes into labels), converts every column, gives the unmatched `9` a label with **Add to list**, opens the preview and closes it with Escape, and creates the linked dataset. The linked dataset's preview shows labels, its rail names the dataset it reads, and the code-list popover says the values were converted. The source's rail names the linked dataset. Then the owner relabels `2` on the dictionary, and the linked dataset shows the new label without a reload: the dictionary save refreshes the rows (Task 23) and the projection key rebuilds the view (Task 10). The only database reads are the final oracle and the cleanup. The agent is not asked anything: Task 24's eval covers how it reads converted columns.

The dictionary is seeded with `1 Male` and `2 Female` only, so the 3 rows with `9` are unmatched. The workspace owner is a workspace admin, so the linked-dataset card is enabled (owner question 8).

The selectors follow the copy of spec sections 7.5 and 13 that Tasks 17 to 21 render: the global switch's **Convert all** (a `SegmentedControl`, so a radio), the footer's **Next: unmatched values** and **Next: save as** (slice 3's `Next: <step>` pattern), the unmatched value's row in **Values being converted** with its **Add to list** option and label input, **Preview data** opening a region of that name, the **Create a new linked dataset** card (a radio), its **Name** field, and **Create linked dataset**. If Tasks 17 to 21 name one differently, use their name here rather than changing their copy.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the spec.** `tests/e2e/dictionary-apply-linked.spec.ts`:

```ts
/*
 * A workspace owner imports a coded line list, converts it into a linked
 * dataset from the dataset's menu, and reads the labels back on the linked
 * dataset's page and rails. Relabelling a code on the dictionary reaches the
 * linked dataset without a reload. The imported dataset is a precondition and
 * the dictionary is seeded before the first page load. Everything the test
 * creates is deleted afterwards.
 */
import { expect, test as base } from "./fixtures/e2e.fixture";
import { signInWithEmailPassword } from "./helpers/auth";
import {
  MEASLES_LINE_LIST_CSV_EXPECTED_ROW_COUNT,
  MEASLES_LINE_LIST_CSV_PATH,
} from "./helpers/constants";
import { deleteDatasetFixture } from "./helpers/deleteDatasetFixture";
import { importDatasetViaUi } from "./helpers/importDatasetViaUi";
import { seedDataDictionary } from "./helpers/seedDataDictionary";
import {
  createSupabaseAdminClient,
  getWorkspaceIdBySlug,
} from "./helpers/supabaseAdminClient";
import { LONG_WAIT, MEDIUM_WAIT } from "./helpers/timeouts";
import type { AvaSupabaseDBClient } from "$/types/AvaSupabaseDbClient.types";
import type { SeedEntry } from "./helpers/seedDataDictionary";
import type { Page } from "@playwright/test";

const DICTIONARY_NAME = "E2E line list codes to convert";

/** Sex without 9, so the line list's three 9s are unmatched. */
const ENTRIES: readonly SeedEntry[] = [
  {
    name: "sex",
    columnNames: ["GENDER"],
    kind: "categorical",
    description: "Sex recorded on the case report.",
    codeList: {
      name: "Sex (1/2)",
      pairs: [
        { code: "1", label: "Male", acceptedSpellings: [], isMissing: false },
        { code: "2", label: "Female", acceptedSpellings: [], isMissing: false },
      ],
    },
  },
  {
    name: "hospitalized",
    columnNames: ["hosp_yn"],
    kind: "categorical",
    codeList: {
      name: "Yes/No",
      pairs: [
        { code: "Y", label: "Yes", acceptedSpellings: [], isMissing: false },
        { code: "N", label: "No", acceptedSpellings: [], isMissing: false },
      ],
    },
  },
];

/** Opens Apply from the menu, which now promises to convert. */
async function _openApply(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "More dataset actions" }).click();
  const applyItem = page.getByRole("menuitem", { name: /Apply a dictionary/ });
  await expect(applyItem).toContainText(
    "Turn codes into labels and add column descriptions",
  );
  await applyItem.click();
}

/** Waits for the matches, then converts every coded column. */
async function _convertAll(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  const genderRow = page.getByRole("row").filter({
    has: page.getByRole("button", { name: "GENDER", exact: true }),
  });
  await expect(genderRow.getByRole("button", { pressed: true })).toContainText(
    "Sex (1/2)",
    { timeout: LONG_WAIT },
  );
  await page.getByText("Convert all", { exact: true }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("radio", { name: "Convert all" })).toBeChecked();
}

/** Labels GENDER's 9, three rows, with Add to list. */
async function _labelUnmatchedNine(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Next: unmatched values" }).click();
  const section = page.getByRole("region", { name: "Values being converted" });
  const nineRow = section
    .getByRole("row")
    .filter({ hasText: "GENDER" })
    .filter({ has: page.getByRole("cell", { name: "9", exact: true }) });
  await expect(nineRow).toContainText("3", { timeout: MEDIUM_WAIT });
  await nineRow.getByText("Add to list", { exact: true }).click();
  await nineRow.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Label for 9" }).fill("Unknown");
}

/** Opens the preview, sees a label, and closes it from the keyboard. */
async function _previewAndClose(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  const previewButton = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Preview data" });
  await previewButton.click();
  const preview = page.getByRole("region", { name: "Preview data" });
  await expect(preview).toContainText("Male", { timeout: MEDIUM_WAIT });
  await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
  await expect(preview).toBeHidden();
  await expect(previewButton).toBeFocused();
}

/** Reads the id of the linked dataset that reads `sourceId`, once it exists. */
async function _waitForLinkedDatasetId(
  admin: AvaSupabaseDBClient,
  sourceId: string,
): Promise<string> {
  let linkedId: string | undefined;
  await expect
    .poll(
      async () => {
        const { data } = await admin
          .from("datasets__virtual")
          .select("dataset_id")
          .eq("linked_source_dataset_id", sourceId)
          .throwOnError();
        linkedId = data[0]?.dataset_id;
        return linkedId;
      },
      { timeout: LONG_WAIT },
    )
    .toBeDefined();
  return linkedId!;
}

/** Saves as a new linked dataset with the default name. Returns the name. */
async function _createLinkedDataset(page: Page): Promise<string> {
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Next: save as" }).click();
  await expect(
    page.getByRole("radio", { name: /Create a new linked dataset/ }),
  ).toBeChecked();
  const nameInput = page.getByLabel("Name", { exact: true });
  await expect(nameInput).toHaveValue(/\(labeled\)$/);
  const linkedName = await nameInput.inputValue();
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Create linked dataset" }).click();
  return linkedName;
}

/** The linked dataset's page: labels, its source, and the popover. */
async function _expectLinkedDatasetPage(
  page: Page,
  sourceName: string,
): Promise<void> {
  await expect(page.getByRole("gridcell", { name: "Female" }).first()).toBeVisible({
    timeout: LONG_WAIT,
  });
  await expect(page.getByRole("gridcell", { name: "Unknown" }).first()).toBeVisible();
  // The rail's Reads fact, since the list pane links to the source too.
  await expect(
    page.getByRole("definition").filter({ hasText: sourceName }),
  ).toBeVisible();
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Code list for GENDER" }).focus();
  await expect(
    page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Code list for GENDER" }),
  ).toContainText("The values were converted to these labels.");
  await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
}

/** Relabels 2 on the dictionary, then opens the linked dataset from Used by. */
async function _relabelFemaleThenOpenLinked(
  page: Page,
  linkedName: string,
): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByRole("link", { name: DICTIONARY_NAME }).first().click();
  await page.getByRole("tab", { name: /Code lists/ }).click();
  const codeLists = page.getByRole("tabpanel", { name: /Code lists/ });
  await codeLists.getByText("Sex (1/2)", { exact: true }).click();
  await codeLists.getByLabel("Label 2").fill("Woman");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Save changes" }).click();
  await expect(page.getByText("Dictionary saved")).toBeVisible({
    timeout: MEDIUM_WAIT,
  });
  await page.getByRole("tab", { name: /Used by/ }).click();
  const linkedRow = page.getByRole("row", { name: new RegExp(linkedName) });
  await expect(linkedRow).toContainText("Linked");
  await linkedRow.getByRole("link", { name: linkedName }).click();
}

/** The seeded dictionary, and the line list a test imports through the UI. */
type LineListFixture = {
  admin: AvaSupabaseDBClient;
  /** Signs in and imports the line list. Returns the dataset id. */
  signInAndImport: () => Promise<string>;
};

/**
 * Seeds the dictionary before the first page load. Afterwards it deletes
 * every linked dataset that reads the import, the import, then the
 * dictionary, whose children cascade.
 */
const test = base.extend<{ lineList: LineListFixture }>({
  lineList: async ({ page, e2eWorkerDb }, use) => {
    const admin = createSupabaseAdminClient();
    const workspaceId = await getWorkspaceIdBySlug({
      supabaseAdminClient: admin,
      slug: e2eWorkerDb.workspaceSlug,
    });
    const dictionaryId = await seedDataDictionary({
      admin,
      workspaceId,
      name: DICTIONARY_NAME,
      entries: ENTRIES,
    });
    let datasetId: string | undefined;
    const signInAndImport = async (): Promise<string> => {
      await signInWithEmailPassword(page, {
        email: e2eWorkerDb.primaryUser.email,
        password: e2eWorkerDb.primaryUser.password,
        workspaceSlug: e2eWorkerDb.workspaceSlug,
      });
      datasetId = await importDatasetViaUi({
        page,
        filePath: MEASLES_LINE_LIST_CSV_PATH,
        expectedRowCount: MEASLES_LINE_LIST_CSV_EXPECTED_ROW_COUNT,
        workspaceSlug: e2eWorkerDb.workspaceSlug,
      });
      return datasetId;
    };
    try {
      await use({ admin, signInAndImport });
    } finally {
      if (datasetId) {
        const { data: linked } = await admin
          .from("datasets__virtual")
          .select("dataset_id")
          .eq("linked_source_dataset_id", datasetId)
          .throwOnError();
        for (const row of linked) {
          await deleteDatasetFixture({
            admin,
            datasetId: row.dataset_id,
            workspaceId,
          });
        }
        await deleteDatasetFixture({ admin, datasetId, workspaceId });
      }
      await admin
        .from("data_dictionaries")
        .delete()
        .eq("id", dictionaryId)
        .throwOnError();
    }
  },
});

test.describe("converting into a linked dataset", () => {
  test("a linked dataset holds labels and follows the dictionary", async ({
    page,
    lineList,
  }) => {
    const { admin } = lineList;
    const sourceId = await lineList.signInAndImport();
    const { data: source } = await admin
      .from("datasets")
      .select("name")
      .eq("id", sourceId)
      .single()
      .throwOnError();

    await _openApply(page);
    await _convertAll(page);
    await _labelUnmatchedNine(page);
    await _previewAndClose(page);
    const linkedName = await _createLinkedDataset(page);
    const linkedId = await _waitForLinkedDatasetId(admin, sourceId);
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(linkedId), { timeout: LONG_WAIT });
    await _expectLinkedDatasetPage(page, source.name);

    await page.getByRole("link", { name: source.name }).first().click();
    await expect(page.getByText(`Linked dataset: ${linkedName}`)).toBeVisible({
      timeout: MEDIUM_WAIT,
    });

    await _relabelFemaleThenOpenLinked(page, linkedName);
    await expect(page.getByRole("gridcell", { name: "Woman" }).first()).toBeVisible({
      timeout: LONG_WAIT,
    });

    const { data: bindings } = await admin
      .from("dataset_columns__dictionary_bindings")
      .select("dataset_id, mode, pinned_pairs")
      .in("dataset_id", [sourceId, linkedId])
      .throwOnError();
    expect(
      bindings
        .map((binding) => {
          const owner = binding.dataset_id === linkedId ? "linked" : "source";
          return `${owner}:${binding.mode}:${binding.pinned_pairs === null}`;
        })
        .sort(),
    ).toEqual([
      "linked:convert:true",
      "linked:convert:true",
      "source:reference:true",
      "source:reference:true",
    ]);
  });
});
```

  (The Code lists tab lists each list as a `NavLink` named by its list and opens the first on its own, so the test picks `Sex (1/2)` by its text.)

### Task 28: Client: re-apply

Re-applying re-pins one dictionary's pinned bindings on one dataset to the list's current pairs and the dictionary's current version, through `rpc_dataset_columns__reapply_dictionary` (Task 4). It changes what a converted column shows, and can change its type, so a success refreshes the bindings, the dataset's columns, and every query showing dataset rows; Task 10's projection key then rebuilds the loaded view. Writes need a connection (spec 12), so offline it says so and sends nothing. A second press while one is in flight is ignored.

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the hook.** `src/hooks/dataDictionaries/useReapplyDictionary/useReapplyDictionary.ts`:

```ts
import { getIsOnline } from "@avandar/browser-utils";
import { useLingui } from "@lingui/react/macro";
import { useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useRef } from "react";
import { DictionaryBinding } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DictionaryBinding/DictionaryBinding";
import { DictionaryBindingClient } from "@/clients/dataDictionaries/DictionaryBindingClient";
import { DatasetColumnClient } from "@/clients/datasets/DatasetColumnClient";
import { Logger } from "@/utils/Logger";
import { notifyError, notifySuccess } from "@/utils/notifications/notify";
import { invalidateDatasetRowQueries } from "@/views/DataManagerApp/DatasetMetaView/invalidateDatasetRowQueries/invalidateDatasetRowQueries";
import type { DataDictionary } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionary/DataDictionary";
import type { Dataset } from "$/models/datasets/Dataset/Dataset";

type ReapplyNames = { datasetName: string; dictionaryName: string };

/** The toast for a refused re-apply, from the RPC's hint. */
function useReapplyErrorMessage({
  datasetName,
  dictionaryName,
}: Readonly<ReapplyNames>): (error: unknown) => string {
  const { t } = useLingui();
  return (error) => {
    switch (DictionaryBinding.toApplyErrorHint(error)) {
      case "dataset_editor_required":
        return t`You need edit access to ${datasetName} to re-apply a dictionary.`;
      case "dictionary_viewer_required":
        return t`You can no longer read ${dictionaryName}, so it was not re-applied.`;
      case "nothing_to_reapply":
        return t`${datasetName} already has the current version of ${dictionaryName}.`;
      default:
        return t`${dictionaryName} was not re-applied to ${datasetName}. Please try again.`;
    }
  };
}

/** Refreshes everything a re-apply changes. */
function useRefreshAfterReapply(): () => Promise<void> {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  return async () => {
    await Promise.all([
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({
        queryKey: [DictionaryBindingClient.getClientName()],
      }),
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({
        queryKey: [DatasetColumnClient.getClientName()],
      }),
      invalidateDatasetRowQueries(queryClient),
    ]);
  };
}

/**
 * Re-applies one dictionary to one dataset converted in place: its pinned
 * columns take the dictionary's current pairs and version. A success
 * refreshes the bindings, the dataset's columns, and the shown rows, and
 * toasts. Offline it says to reconnect and sends nothing. A second call
 * while one is in flight is ignored. Used by Re-apply in the Dictionary
 * view's Used by tab and the dataset rail.
 */
export function useReapplyDictionary(
  options: Readonly<
    ReapplyNames & { datasetId: Dataset.Id; dictionaryId: DataDictionary.Id }
  >,
): [reapply: () => void, isReapplying: boolean] {
  const { t } = useLingui();
  const { datasetName, dictionaryName } = options;
  const toErrorMessage = useReapplyErrorMessage(options);
  const refresh = useRefreshAfterReapply();
  const isReapplyingRef = useRef(false);
  const [reapplyDictionary, isReapplying] =
    DictionaryBindingClient.useReapplyDictionary({
      onSuccess: async () => {
        await refresh();
        notifySuccess(t`Re-applied ${dictionaryName} to ${datasetName}.`);
      },
      onError: (error: unknown) => {
        Logger.error(error, { devMsg: "Re-applying a dictionary failed" });
        notifyError(toErrorMessage(error));
      },
      onSettled: () => {
        isReapplyingRef.current = false;
      },
    });
  const reapply = (): void => {
    if (!getIsOnline()) {
      notifyError(t`You're offline. Reconnect to save this.`);
      return;
    }
    if (isReapplyingRef.current) {
      return;
    }
    isReapplyingRef.current = true;
    reapplyDictionary({
      datasetId: options.datasetId,
      dictionaryId: options.dictionaryId,
    });
  };
  return [reapply, isReapplying];
}
```

```ts
/** Whether any column of the dataset can be converted at all. */
export function canConvert(targets: Readonly<ApplyTargets>): boolean {
  return (
    targets.isLinkedDataset ||
    targets.linked.isAvailable ||
    targets.inPlace.isAvailable
  );
}

/**
 * The card the Save step opens with: Change for a dataset already
 * converted in place, else a new linked dataset when one can be created,
 * else Change. A linked dataset has no cards, so it has no target.
 */
export function getDefaultSaveTarget(
  targets: Readonly<ApplyTargets>,
): SaveTarget | undefined {
  if (targets.isLinkedDataset) {
    return undefined;
  }
  if (targets.isAlreadyConvertedInPlace && targets.inPlace.isAvailable) {
    return "in_place";
  }
  if (targets.linked.isAvailable) {
    return "linked";
  }
  return targets.inPlace.isAvailable ? "in_place" : undefined;
}
```

```tsx
import { useLingui } from "@lingui/react/macro";
import { Group, Radio, Stack, Text } from "@mantine/core";
import { useId } from "react";
import { useDatasetSourceLabels } from "@/hooks/datasets/useDatasetSourceLabels";
import css from "@/views/DataManagerApp/ApplyDictionariesView/SaveAsStep/SaveAsStep.module.css";
import type { Dataset } from "$/models/datasets/Dataset/Dataset";
import type { ApplyTargets } from "@/views/DataManagerApp/ApplyDictionariesView/applyTargets/applyTargets";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

type Props = {
  dataset: Dataset.T;
  inPlace: ApplyTargets["inPlace"];
};

/** What changing in place does, or why it is not possible here. */
function useDescription(dataset: Dataset.T, inPlace: ApplyTargets["inPlace"]): string {
  const { t } = useLingui();
  const sourceLabels = useDatasetSourceLabels();
  const datasetName = dataset.name;
  const sourceName = sourceLabels[dataset.sourceType];
  if (inPlace.isAvailable) {
    return inPlace.storage === "synced"
      ? t`Rewrites the uploaded data in place. It is synced to the workspace, so this changes it for everyone who uses it.`
      : t`It is offline only, so nobody else is affected.`;
  }
  if (inPlace.reason === "has_linked_datasets") {
    return t`A linked dataset reads ${datasetName}, so it can't be changed in place. Convert in the linked dataset instead.`;
  }
  return dataset.sourceType === "virtual"
    ? t`${datasetName} is built from other data, so a linked dataset is the only option.`
    : t`${sourceName} data can't be changed from Avandar yet, so a linked dataset is the only option for now.`;
}

/**
 * The Change <dataset> card: converts the dataset itself, pinned to the
 * dictionary versions applied. Its copy depends on where the data lives,
 * and it is disabled, saying why, where changing in place is not possible.
 */
export function ChangeDatasetCard({ dataset, inPlace }: Readonly<Props>): ReactNode {
  const { t } = useLingui();
  const titleId = useId();
  const descriptionId = useId();
  const description = useDescription(dataset, inPlace);
  const datasetName = dataset.name;
  return (
    <Radio.Card
      value="in_place"
      disabled={!inPlace.isAvailable}
      className={css.saveTargetCard}
      aria-labelledby={titleId}
      aria-describedby={descriptionId}
    >
      <Group wrap="nowrap" align="flex-start" gap="sm">
        <Radio.Indicator disabled={!inPlace.isAvailable} />
        <Stack gap={2}>
          <Text id={titleId} fw={600} size="sm">
            {t`Change ${datasetName}`}
          </Text>
          <Text id={descriptionId} size="xs" c="dimmed">
            {description}
          </Text>
        </Stack>
      </Group>
    </Radio.Card>
  );
}
```

### Task 30: Re-apply in Used by and the rail

**Re-apply** appears where a dataset converted in place is behind its dictionary: in the dictionary's Used by tab, beside "Applied version 2, now version 3", and in the dataset's rail, as the rail's one action (owner question 2). Both show only to someone who can edit the dataset: Used by reads the workspace's editable dataset ids once (F132's `rpc_datasets__get_editable_ids`), and the rail reads the viewer's role on its own dataset. A synced upload asks first, since re-applying changes it for everyone ("This changes <dataset> for everyone in the workspace who uses it."); an offline-only upload re-applies at once. The button's visible text, "Re-apply", starts its accessible name, which also names the dictionary and the dataset.

```tsx
import { Trans, useLingui } from "@lingui/react/macro";
import { Button, Text } from "@mantine/core";
import { modals } from "@mantine/modals";
import { DatasetClient } from "@/clients/datasets/DatasetClient/DatasetClient";
import { useReapplyDictionary } from "@/hooks/dataDictionaries/useReapplyDictionary/useReapplyDictionary";
import type { DataDictionary } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionary/DataDictionary";
import type { Dataset } from "$/models/datasets/Dataset/Dataset";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

type Props = {
  dataset: Pick<Dataset.T, "id" | "name" | "sourceType">;
  dictionaryId: DataDictionary.Id;
  dictionaryName: string;
};

/**
 * Whether re-applying changes the dataset for the whole workspace: true
 * for an upload synced to the cloud, and while its source is still being
 * read, so the question is asked rather than skipped.
 */
function useChangesWorkspace(dataset: Props["dataset"]): boolean {
  const [source] = DatasetClient.useGetSourceDataset({
    datasetId: dataset.id,
    sourceType: dataset.sourceType,
  });
  return !source || !("isInCloudStorage" in source) || source.isInCloudStorage;
}

/**
 * Re-applies a dictionary to a dataset converted in place, so its pinned
 * columns take the dictionary's current version. Asks first when the
 * dataset is synced to the workspace. Shown wherever a dataset is behind
 * its dictionary, for someone who can edit the dataset: the Used by tab
 * and the dataset rail.
 */
export function ReapplyButton({
  dataset,
  dictionaryId,
  dictionaryName,
}: Readonly<Props>): ReactNode {
  const { t } = useLingui();
  const datasetName = dataset.name;
  const changesWorkspace = useChangesWorkspace(dataset);
  const [reapply, isReapplying] = useReapplyDictionary({
    datasetId: dataset.id,
    datasetName,
    dictionaryId,
    dictionaryName,
  });
  const onClick = (): void => {
    if (!changesWorkspace) {
      reapply();
      return;
    }
    modals.openConfirmModal({
      title: t`Re-apply ${dictionaryName}?`,
      children: (
        <Text size="sm">
          <Trans>
            This changes {datasetName} for everyone in the workspace who uses
            it.
          </Trans>
        </Text>
      ),
      labels: { confirm: t`Re-apply`, cancel: t`Cancel` },
      onConfirm: reapply,
    });
  };
  return (
    <Button
      size="compact-xs"
      variant="light"
      loading={isReapplying}
      onClick={onClick}
      aria-label={t`Re-apply ${dictionaryName} to ${datasetName}`}
    >
      <Trans>Re-apply</Trans>
    </Button>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * One row per dataset the dictionary is applied to, and how, with
 * Re-apply on a dataset that is behind and that the user can edit.
 */
export function DictionaryUsedByTable({ usage }: Readonly<Props>): ReactNode {
  const workspace = useCurrentWorkspace();
  const [editableIds] = DatasetClient.useGetEditableIds({
    workspaceId: workspace.id,
  });
  const editableIdSet = new Set<string>(editableIds ?? []);
  return (
    <Table layout="fixed" verticalSpacing="xs">
      <Table.Thead>
        <Table.Tr>
          <Table.Th>
            <Trans>Dataset</Trans>
          </Table.Th>
          <Table.Th w="40%">
            <Trans>How it was applied</Trans>
          </Table.Th>
          <Table.Th w="10%" ta="end">
            <Trans>Entries</Trans>
          </Table.Th>
          <Table.Th w="22%">
            <Trans>Status</Trans>
          </Table.Th>
        </Table.Tr>
      </Table.Thead>
      <Table.Tbody>
        {usage.rows.map((row) => {
          return (
            <UsageRow
              key={row.datasetId}
              row={row}
              usage={usage}
              canEdit={editableIdSet.has(row.datasetId)}
            />
          );
        })}
      </Table.Tbody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

### Task 31: End-to-end: converting in place

One test, driven through the UI with only the dictionary seeded before the first page load. A workspace owner imports the line list (synced to the cloud), converts it in place: **Change <dataset>** with its warning, whose button stays disabled until "I understand this changes <dataset> for the whole workspace" is ticked. The dataset's own preview shows labels and its rail says "Converted this dataset · version 1". Relabelling `2` on the dictionary does not reach it (it is pinned): Used by says "Changed the data" and "Applied version 1, now version 2", and so does the rail. **Re-apply** in the rail asks first (a synced upload), and the new label arrives. The only database reads are the final oracle and the cleanup.

The selectors follow spec 7.5's copy that Task 29 renders: the **Change <dataset>** card (a radio), its confirmation checkbox, and **Change 1 column**. The Unmatched values step has nothing to show (every value has a label), so its button only moves on. If Task 29 names one differently, use its name here rather than changing its copy.

**Files:**
- Create: `tests/e2e/dictionary-apply-in-place.spec.ts`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the spec.** `tests/e2e/dictionary-apply-in-place.spec.ts`:

```ts
/*
 * A workspace owner imports a coded line list and converts it in place from
 * the dataset's menu, after confirming it changes the dataset for the whole
 * workspace. The conversion is pinned: relabelling a code on the dictionary
 * shows the dataset as behind until Re-apply. The imported dataset is a
 * precondition and the dictionary is seeded before the first page load.
 * Everything the test creates is deleted afterwards.
 */
import { expect, test as base } from "./fixtures/e2e.fixture";
import { signInWithEmailPassword } from "./helpers/auth";
import {
  MEASLES_LINE_LIST_CSV_EXPECTED_ROW_COUNT,
  MEASLES_LINE_LIST_CSV_PATH,
} from "./helpers/constants";
import { deleteDatasetFixture } from "./helpers/deleteDatasetFixture";
import { importDatasetViaUi } from "./helpers/importDatasetViaUi";
import { seedDataDictionary } from "./helpers/seedDataDictionary";
import {
  createSupabaseAdminClient,
  getWorkspaceIdBySlug,
} from "./helpers/supabaseAdminClient";
import { LONG_WAIT, MEDIUM_WAIT } from "./helpers/timeouts";
import type { AvaSupabaseDBClient } from "$/types/AvaSupabaseDbClient.types";
import type { SeedEntry } from "./helpers/seedDataDictionary";
import type { Page } from "@playwright/test";

const DICTIONARY_NAME = "E2E line list codes to change in place";

const ENTRIES: readonly SeedEntry[] = [
  {
    name: "sex",
    columnNames: ["GENDER"],
    kind: "categorical",
    codeList: {
      name: "Sex (1/2/9)",
      pairs: [
        { code: "1", label: "Male", acceptedSpellings: [], isMissing: false },
        { code: "2", label: "Female", acceptedSpellings: [], isMissing: false },
        { code: "9", label: "Unknown", acceptedSpellings: [], isMissing: true },
      ],
    },
  },
];

/** Converts GENDER in place, ticking the workspace-wide warning. */
async function _convertInPlace(page: Page, datasetName: string): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "More dataset actions" }).click();
  await page.getByRole("menuitem", { name: /Apply a dictionary/ }).click();
  const genderRow = page.getByRole("row").filter({
    has: page.getByRole("button", { name: "GENDER", exact: true }),
  });
  await expect(genderRow.getByRole("button", { pressed: true })).toContainText(
    "Sex (1/2/9)",
    { timeout: LONG_WAIT },
  );
  await page.getByText("Convert all", { exact: true }).click();
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Next: unmatched values" }).click();
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Next: save as" }).click();
  await page.getByText(`Change ${datasetName}`, { exact: true }).click();
  const changeButton = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Change 1 column" });
  await expect(changeButton).toBeDisabled();
  await page
    .getByLabel(`I understand this changes ${datasetName} for the whole workspace`)
    .check();
  await expect(changeButton).toBeEnabled();
  await changeButton.click();
}

/** Relabels 2 on the dictionary from the dataset's rail. */
async function _relabelFemale(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByRole("link", { name: DICTIONARY_NAME }).first().click();
  await page.getByRole("tab", { name: /Code lists/ }).click();
  const codeLists = page.getByRole("tabpanel", { name: /Code lists/ });
  await codeLists.getByLabel("Label 2").fill("Woman");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Save changes" }).click();
  await expect(page.getByText("Dictionary saved")).toBeVisible({
    timeout: MEDIUM_WAIT,
  });
}

/** Used by says the dataset is behind; opens the dataset from there. */
async function _expectBehindInUsedBy(
  page: Page,
  datasetName: string,
): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByRole("tab", { name: /Used by/ }).click();
  const row = page.getByRole("row", { name: new RegExp(datasetName) });
  await expect(row).toContainText("Changed the data");
  await expect(row).toContainText("Applied version 1, now version 2");
  await row.getByRole("link", { name: datasetName }).click();
}

/** Re-applies from the rail, confirming the workspace-wide change. */
async function _reapplyFromRail(page: Page, datasetName: string): Promise<void> {
  await page
    .getByRole("button", { name: `Re-apply ${DICTIONARY_NAME} to ${datasetName}` })
    .click();
  const dialog = page.getByRole("dialog");
  await expect(dialog).toContainText(
    `This changes ${datasetName} for everyone in the workspace who uses it.`,
  );
  await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Re-apply", exact: true }).click();
  await expect(
    page.getByText(`Re-applied ${DICTIONARY_NAME} to ${datasetName}.`),
  ).toBeVisible({ timeout: MEDIUM_WAIT });
}

/** The seeded dictionary, and the line list a test imports through the UI. */
type LineListFixture = {
  admin: AvaSupabaseDBClient;
  /** Signs in and imports the line list. Returns the dataset id. */
  signInAndImport: () => Promise<string>;
};

/**
 * Seeds the dictionary before the first page load. Afterwards it deletes
 * the imported dataset, then the dictionary, whose children cascade.
 */
const test = base.extend<{ lineList: LineListFixture }>({
  lineList: async ({ page, e2eWorkerDb }, use) => {
    const admin = createSupabaseAdminClient();
    const workspaceId = await getWorkspaceIdBySlug({
      supabaseAdminClient: admin,
      slug: e2eWorkerDb.workspaceSlug,
    });
    const dictionaryId = await seedDataDictionary({
      admin,
      workspaceId,
      name: DICTIONARY_NAME,
      entries: ENTRIES,
    });
    let datasetId: string | undefined;
    const signInAndImport = async (): Promise<string> => {
      await signInWithEmailPassword(page, {
        email: e2eWorkerDb.primaryUser.email,
        password: e2eWorkerDb.primaryUser.password,
        workspaceSlug: e2eWorkerDb.workspaceSlug,
      });
      datasetId = await importDatasetViaUi({
        page,
        filePath: MEASLES_LINE_LIST_CSV_PATH,
        expectedRowCount: MEASLES_LINE_LIST_CSV_EXPECTED_ROW_COUNT,
        workspaceSlug: e2eWorkerDb.workspaceSlug,
      });
      return datasetId;
    };
    try {
      await use({ admin, signInAndImport });
    } finally {
      if (datasetId) {
        await deleteDatasetFixture({ admin, datasetId, workspaceId });
      }
      await admin
        .from("data_dictionaries")
        .delete()
        .eq("id", dictionaryId)
        .throwOnError();
    }
  },
});

test.describe("converting a dataset in place", () => {
  test("a dataset converted in place keeps its version until Re-apply", async ({
    page,
    lineList,
  }) => {
    const { admin } = lineList;
    const datasetId = await lineList.signInAndImport();
    const { data: dataset } = await admin
      .from("datasets")
      .select("name")
      .eq("id", datasetId)
      .single()
      .throwOnError();

    await _convertInPlace(page, dataset.name);
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(datasetId), { timeout: LONG_WAIT });
    await expect(page.getByRole("gridcell", { name: "Female" }).first()).toBeVisible({
      timeout: LONG_WAIT,
    });
    await expect(
      page.getByText("Converted this dataset · version 1"),
    ).toBeVisible();

    await _relabelFemale(page);
    await _expectBehindInUsedBy(page, dataset.name);
    await expect(page.getByRole("gridcell", { name: "Female" }).first()).toBeVisible({
      timeout: LONG_WAIT,
    });
    await expect(page.getByText("Applied version 1, now version 2")).toBeVisible();

    await _reapplyFromRail(page, dataset.name);
    await expect(page.getByRole("gridcell", { name: "Woman" }).first()).toBeVisible({
      timeout: LONG_WAIT,
    });
    await expect(
      page.getByText("Converted this dataset · version 2"),
    ).toBeVisible();

    const { data: binding } = await admin
      .from("dataset_columns__dictionary_bindings")
      .select("mode, applied_dictionary_version, pinned_pairs")
      .eq("dataset_id", datasetId)
      .single()
      .throwOnError();
    expect(binding.mode).toBe("convert");
    expect(binding.applied_dictionary_version).toBe(2);
    expect(JSON.stringify(binding.pinned_pairs)).toContain('"Woman"');
  });
});
```

## Executing this plan in batches

The tasks are ordered so each batch can go to one subagent, which runs its tasks one at a time ("any order" means the order within that one subagent), with independent batches in parallel. No two batches that run alongside each other change the same file. Task 0 runs first, by the coordinating session. Parallel batches share one worktree: each commits only its own paths, by name, and retries a commit that meets `index.lock`.

| Batch | Tasks | Needs | Runs alongside |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T: templating | 1 | Task 0 | S |
| S: schema | 2, 3, 4, then 5 | Task 0, with `ava supabase status` naming `feat-dictionary-conversions` | T |
| M: shared models | 6, then 7 | S (Task 5's generated types) | none |
| R: rendering and loading | 8, 9 (in order), then 10, 11, 12 (any order) | T, M | C |
| C: column codes | 13 | M | R |
| U: apply flow | 14, 15, 16 (in order), then 17, 18, 19 (any order), then 20, 21 | M, and R's Task 9 (`ava_raw_` views) | D |
| D: dataset page and Used by | 22, 23 | C, and R's Task 9 (`ava_raw_` view names for the unlabeled count) | U |
| E: eval | 24 | C, R | F |
| F: e2e | 25 | U, D, R | E |
| G: finish Part A | 26, then 27 | E, F | none |
| B: Part B | 28, then 29 and 30 (any order), then 31, 32, 33 | G, or the merged Part A | none |

Every batch ends with its own tests green and a commit per task. Review between batches with the `avandar-code-review` skill.

## Refinements made while planning

These override the spec where they differ.

- **An ordered list's `ENUM` is built when the relation loads.** Spec 6.4 cast the decoded output to an `ENUM` of the list's labels. Run on the browser's DuckDB, that cast fails every query once one value is not a listed label, `TRY_CAST` silently empties the value, and duplicate labels refuse the type. The `ENUM` is the list's non-blank labels in list order, then the values the conversion keeps, read with one `SELECT DISTINCT` at load (Tasks 8, 9). The `VARCHAR` plus sort-key fallback of spec 18.1 is not needed.
- **Encoded integers are `BIGINT`, not `INTEGER`.** Ava's integer type is `bigint`, so a `BIGINT` view column and `dataset_columns.data_type = 'bigint'` agree. A code with more than 18 digits makes the output `varchar`.
- **`valueMapping` is a `ColumnConversion.T`.** Spec 6.2's `ColumnValueMapping` (pairs, direction, overrides, keep-original name, output type) is the shared `ColumnConversion` model, so the view, the apply flow's preview and unmatched-value queries, and the tests render one set of rules. The output type is read from the column's stored `data_type` (plus `isOrdered` for the `ENUM`), so the view never disagrees with the schema the agent and the query builder see.
- **Both sides of a match are normalized by DuckDB.** The `WHEN` literals are `lower(trim('<literal>'))`, not keys lowercased in TypeScript, so Unicode case rules can never differ between the key and the data.
- **Blank labels.** Decoding skips a pair with a blank label: its code passes through and is listed in Unmatched values, where Add to list is disabled ("This value is in the list without a label. Label it on the dictionary."). Encoding ignores the blank label but still matches the pair's accepted spellings. `ENUM` labels skip blanks (spec 5.1 left this to slice 4).
- **The binding stores two more columns.** `pinned_is_ordered` keeps a pinned list's order with its pairs, and `replaced_data_type` remembers the column's type before converting, so removing the binding or switching the column to Reference only restores it exactly (spec 6.3 restored `detected_data_type`, which forgets a type the user chose).
- **A keep-original copy is a `dataset_columns` row that shares the converted column's `original_name`.** Its Parquet header is the converted column's, so column-subset loading maps a query naming `GENDER_original` to the `GENDER` header with no extra rule. Its name is `<name>_original`, then `_2`, `_3` when taken, and renaming it is allowed (the projection reads its current name).
- **Converted types are read-only on the dataset page.** The Type cell of a converted column says "Set by <dictionary>": the type follows the conversion.
- **Code-list deletion pins live convert bindings.** Spec 14 pinned a linked dataset's conversions when its dictionary or entry was deleted; a deleted code list now does the same, so no linked dataset stops converting silently. A reference binding is re-pointed in the same save when its entry is left exactly one code list (open decision 5, owner question 4).
- **The dictionary save re-derives converted types.** A live convert binding's output type follows its list (a new non-integer code turns `bigint` into `varchar`), so `rpc_data_dictionaries__save` updates those columns' `data_type` in the same transaction.
- **A linked dataset is created by its own RPC.** Spec 5.5 had `rpc_dataset_columns__apply_dictionaries` call `rpc_datasets__add_virtual_dataset` first. A separate `rpc_dataset_columns__apply_dictionaries_as_linked_dataset` keeps one transaction (a refusal leaves no dataset behind) and builds the new dataset's columns from the source's on the server, so the client cannot describe them wrongly.
- **Only workspace admins create linked datasets.** Every dataset insert goes through `rpc_datasets__add_dataset`, which requires `util__can_manage_workspace_settings`. Anyone else sees the linked card disabled with "Only workspace admins can add datasets." (owner question 8).
- **Applying to a linked dataset saves in place, live.** Its Save step has no cards: the button reads **Update <dataset>** and its conversions keep following the dictionaries. A non-linked virtual dataset and a live connection can only convert into a new linked dataset.
- **A raw-values view.** A converted dataset's view holds labels, but profiling, matching, unmatched values, and the preview need the stored values, so every loaded relation also gets `ava_raw_<datasetId>` (renames and casts, no conversions), resolved by the SQL analyzer as a read of the dataset like `ava_rows_`.
- **A loaded view reloads when its projection changes.** Spec 6.2 said bindings are read with the `ensureQueryData` pattern and invalidated on change. `ensureQueryData` returns cached data even after an invalidation, and the queryable tier never rebuilt a loaded view. Each loaded relation records a projection key; bindings and code lists are read with `fetchQuery` (with a fallback to cached data when offline), and a different key rebuilds the view from the storage tier on the next query (open decision 2).
- **Published snapshots read converted datasets through the query.** A dataset with a convert binding counts as having column replacements, so its slices are not copied from the stored file.
- **Virtual dataset freshness is the SQL plus the dependencies.** Spec 9 proposed the virtual row's `updated_at` as the freshness signal. The storage key's definition token is the defining SQL itself (an exact match on what produced the bytes), a virtual dataset's rows go stale when a dependency's do (a linked dataset over a Google Sheet follows the sheet's 5-minute age), and a source's Refresh also clears the linked datasets that read it.
- **No new prompt version.** A converted column's code line is written for the side it holds after conversion (`values Male, Female`), which prompt `data-agent-v5` already reads as stored labels. The `chat` function must be redeployed with the frontend because the shared formatter and the bindings it reads changed (owner question 5).
- **Template parameters are substituted once and literally.** `getQueryStringFromParams` used `String.replace` with a string replacement, one parameter after another, so a label containing `` $` `` could close its quotes in the trusted view statement. It now substitutes in one pass with a replacer function (Task 1).
- **Every workspace query reads the catalog.** The projection key needs each dependency's columns, bindings, and code lists, so a `catalog` session reads them on every query that names a dataset, mostly from the query cache, even when every relation is already loaded. A `stored` session never reads them. When the cached bindings are older than the online stale time, the refetch happens while the query holds its DuckDB lease. When bindings cannot be read and nothing is cached, the dataset loads unconverted, the failure is logged, and the first successful read rebuilds the view.
- **Virtual datasets are acquired once more after this ships.** Cached virtual entries carry no definition token, so each is re-acquired once.
- **Rules the apply RPCs enforce beyond the spec.** Added values go only to a code list the apply uses, trimmed, with no accepted spellings, not marked missing, and bump each touched dictionary's version once. A keep-original copy cannot itself be bound. A linked dataset cannot be the source of another, and must convert at least one column. Copies are named once (`<name>_original`, then `_2`), compared ignoring case, placed after the last column, and keep a user's rename. A two-argument call from a tab opened before the deploy still works through the new parameter's default.
- **Conversion edge rules.** A `map` override to a code no longer in the list is dropped. A blank "Add to list" keeps the value as is. A code already in the list with a blank label cannot be added again; it is labeled on the dictionary. The projection renderer now quotes every identifier with `quoteSqlIdentifier`, which changes no text unless a name holds `"`.
- **A pinned binding whose dictionary or entry is gone, or cannot be read, still converts.** It is listed with `isSourceDeleted`, the Type cell reads "Set by a conversion", and the popover says the dictionary was deleted or is unavailable.
- **The popover and rail copy the spec did not have.** An encoding conversion's popover footer reads "The values were converted to these codes." A linked dataset's own rail line reads "Converted as it loads · follows the dictionary". The unlabeled count stops at 1,000 values.
- **Part A converts only for admins.** Linked datasets are Part A's only conversion target, so a dataset editor who is not a workspace admin sees the convert controls locked with an explanation until Part B lets them convert an upload in place (owner question 24).
- **Re-apply has its own RPC.** `rpc_dataset_columns__reapply_dictionary` re-pins one dictionary's pinned bindings on one dataset without resending the whole set, and asks for a confirmation on a synced dataset (owner question 2).
- **Switching a converted column back to Reference only restores its values.** Stored data is never rewritten, so the Save step's summary says "Back to the original values" for such a column. A separate "Restore original values" action stays on the roadmap (spec 17).
